about: One valid exercise of each critical-thinking type (CONTENT_SPEC.md "Types"): tests/thinking_types.js validates them with engine/packcheck.js and tools/validate.py and plays them in the app.

exercises.q: A student works out the kinetic energy of a 2 kg cart moving at 3 m/s. Which line is wrong, and why?
lines: Kinetic energy is E = ½ · m · v².
So the cart carries 3 J of kinetic energy.
reasons: The mass should be in grams
The ½ belongs only to potential energy
Joules are the wrong unit for energy
exercises.explain: The formula squares the speed, so line 3 must use 3² = 9, which gives E = 9 J. The tempting reasons are wrong: SI mass is in kilograms, and the ½ is part of the kinetic-energy formula itself.

exercises.q: A 1 kg ball is dropped from a 5 m high balcony. Take g = 10 m/s² and ignore air resistance.

parts.q: Its potential energy at the top, relative to the ground, is…
Just before it hits the ground, its kinetic energy is about 50 J.
parts.explain: Without air resistance, all the potential energy turns into kinetic energy.

parts.q: What changes if the ball had a mass of 2 kg?
options: Both energies double, and the speed at the ground stays the same
The speed at the ground doubles
why: Right: E grows with m, but v = √(2gh) does not depend on m.
v = √(2gh) has no m in it.
The kinetic energy at the ground equals the potential energy at the top, so it doubles too.

exercises.explain: Energy is conserved: m·g·h at the top becomes ½·m·v² at the bottom. The mass appears on both sides, so the speed does not depend on it, but both energies do.

exercises.q: A heavy ball and a light ball of the same size are dropped together from 2 m in a room with no air. Which one lands first?
why: Right: every body falls with the same g.
Weight is larger, but so is the inertia; the acceleration is the same.
There is no air to slow the heavy ball down more.
exercises.outcome: They land together after about 0.63 s, because both fall with the same acceleration g ≈ 9.8 m/s².
exercises.explain: Gravity's force grows with mass, and so does the mass that has to be accelerated, so a = F/m = g for every body. The everyday intuition that heavy things fall faster comes from air resistance, and this room has none.

exercises.q: Your measured efficiency of a small generator is 130 %. Walk through the checks.

options.text: That input and output are in the same units
options.fb: Efficiency compares two energies; mixed units are the most common cause.
Over 100 % is impossible, so the measurement is wrong, not the machine.

options.text: Check that input and output cover the same time interval
options.fb: A longer output window inflates the output energy.
That hides the error instead of finding it.

exercises.explain: An efficiency above 100 % always means a measuring error, because a machine cannot give out more energy than it takes in. Check units first, then the time windows, then the instruments.

exercises.q: You suspect your measured fall times are too long because of air resistance. Which single experiment tells you the most?
options: Drop the same ball from several heights and compare with t = √(2h/g)
Drop it once more from the same height
why: Several heights show whether the gap grows with speed, which is the signature of air resistance.
Repeating gives precision, not a test of the cause.
Mass alone does not change the fall time without air.
Temperature barely changes the drag at these speeds.
exercises.explain: Air resistance grows with speed, so its effect grows with the height of the drop. Comparing several heights with the no-air formula separates it from random error; a single repeat cannot.

exercises.q: Claim: solar power should replace coal power stations in a sunny country.

sides.position: For: it emits no CO₂ while running and its fuel is free
counters: It produces nothing at night, so storage or a backup is needed
The sun will burn out tomorrow
why: The real weakness: supply does not follow demand.
False; the sun has billions of years left.

sides.position: Against: coal is reliable day and night
counters: Its CO₂ emissions drive climate change and its fuel costs keep rising
why: The real weakness: emissions and fuel cost.

exercises.explain: A strong objection hits the core of a position: for solar that is intermittency, for coal it is emissions and fuel cost. Weak objections attack details that do not matter to the claim.
